title: Initial-check precision depends on resolved claim scope
body: A 2026-09-10 exploratory trial on elevenlabs/packages at c7c5bdc found useful initial checks without a model: two README snippets failed against real types, and Turbo 2.10.8 kept the widget test hash unchanged after a test-config edit while a source edit changed it. Controls showed why deterministic does not mean correct: a missing lint wrapper was a valid transit task; generated files were absent before build; broad import reachability was not coverage; README command cwd and runtime ranges needed scope review. Existing Mason audit scans only selected instruction files and searches a union of package scripts, so discovery and scope can hide stronger findings. Prefer explicit claims checked against exact package/version/environment evidence. Keep unsupported inputs unavailable and inferred scope advisory; use the connected agent for rationale and ambiguity. Proposed new checks are research recommendations, not shipped capabilities or accepted policy. Full results: .mason/reports/initial-checks-research-2026-09-10/report.md. No population precision or agent-outcome improvement was established.

sources.note: Local research report and reproducible prototypes, with compiler/hash controls; ignored report is not distributed with Git.
Pinned task definitions for hash-input and transit-task observations.
Two complete TypeScript examples checked against actual local exports with TypeScript 5.9.3.
